title: Friendly Error Translation & Provider Abstraction
scope: Map how OpenWorker translates vendor-specific API errors into actionable sentences the LLM can understand — preventing raw error noise from corrupting the conversation.

friendly_model_error.behavior: Returns one actionable sentence for 'account can't use this model' failures, or None for unrecognized. Anything unrecognized returns None → caller surfaces raw error.
friendly_model_error.matching: Matches on error BODY text (error codes/types), not just HTTP status — a 404 also means 'wrong base_url', a 429 also means 'slow down'. Neither dressed up as access problem.
friendly_model_error.no_access_markers: _NO_ACCESS = (model_not_found, does not exist or you do not have access, does not have access to model, permission_error, permission denied)
friendly_model_error.no_quota_markers: _NO_QUOTA = (insufficient_quota, exceeded your current quota, credit balance is too low, billing hard limit)

provider_abc.methods: complete() (non-streaming), stream() (generator yielding StreamChunk), capabilities(model) (ModelCapabilities), close()
provider_abc.contract: The runtime NEVER imports a provider SDK directly — it talks to a ProviderClient. All providers implement the same interface.

token_usage_normalization.model: TokenUsage dataclass (base.py:25): input, output, cache_read, cache_write
token_usage_normalization.context_tokens: property: input + cache_read + cache_write — what actually occupied the window
token_usage_normalization.provider_variance: Providers that don't report cache split (Ollama, most compat) leave cache fields at 0

capabilities_matrix.source: Curated exact-match table for known models; heuristics for ollama/bedrock/vertex/gemini families; custom models fall through to conservative defaults
capabilities_matrix.purpose: Prevents the LLM from attempting vision/PDF on models that don't support it — avoids hallucinated capability assumptions

error_in_engine.context: engine.py:363 — provider failure caught in _loop() try/except around _astream()
error_in_engine.context_overflow: is_context_overflow(exc) routes 400 context-overflow into compaction retry path, not surfaced as error
error_in_engine.friendly: friendly_model_error(self.model, exc) maps to actionable sentence
error_in_engine.persist: _append_notice('error', ...) persists as display-only notice (role='notice', stripped from provider feed) — survives reload
error_in_engine.emit: Event(EventType.ERROR, payload) with error + error_type fields

proposal: ai-factory surfaces raw provider exceptions (ModelHTTPError with vendor JSON bodies) directly to Pydantic-AI, which can emit confusing error text into the LLM context. OpenWorker's friendly_model_error() translates these to actionable sentences ('Your account is out of quota for MODEL — add credits or pick a different model') that the LLM can actually act on. ai-factory should adopt a similar translation layer, plus the ModelCapabilities matrix to prevent the LLM from hallucinating unsupported features.

pydantic_ai_2_impl.pattern: Pydantic output_type for typed error envelope + friendly_model_error translation at the provider boundary — vendor noise becomes actionable LLM context via ToolError.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.why_now: ai-factory's LLMs receive raw ModelHTTPError JSON bodies in their context when provider calls fail — the LLM can't parse vendor-specific error formats and either ignores them or hallucinates a fix. OpenWorker's friendly_model_error (errors.py:38) proves that translating to 'Your account is out of quota for MODEL' gives the LLM actionable context to switch models or report back. This is the kimi-cli KC-03/KC-09 gap: raw openai SDK with no structured error contract.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.harness_gap: Friendly error translation currently lands at factory/common/subprocess.py:83 where _run_tool() wraps non-zero exit stderr into a JSON envelope {success:false, message:stderr} instead of raw text, and at factory/infra/tools_shell.py where ModelRetry raises actionable recovery messages (lines 54, 89, 110). However, unlike OpenWorker's friendly_model_error(), vendor-specific LLM API errors — ModelHTTPError JSON bodies from provider calls — still propagate raw to the agent context with no provider-boundary ErrorClassifier (type/status_code/actionable) translating quota/auth/context-overflow into actionable sentences. No ModelCapabilities matrix exists to prevent hallucinating vision/PDF on unsupported models.
